title: I'm building a realistic sailing game with co-op planned. Early tiller, mainsail and instruments demo
author: GoneSailingDev
selftext:
Hey all,

I sail in real life from time to time in Croatia and thought it would be fun to have a game to go sailing virtually with my friends. Last week I decided to build one myself. Yes, I use Claude Code, and I've also been a professional software developer for over 10 years.

The game is meant to actually simulate the physics of the water and of a sailing boat. The attached short video shows a few features: steering with the tiller, unrolling the mainsail, and the instruments, which show live values (map and depth are still placeholders).

Of course, the game is still at a very early stage, not even alpha. A lot of polish is still needed: graphics, controls, HUD and the synthetic sound effects are all quite rough. First I want to make sure the sailing works and feels like the real thing, so the full focus is on the boat, its physics and its features. Harbours, real maps and different boat types come after that.

I already have many ideas for future features. Co-op is planned, and the game is built to support it from the start.

Feedback is welcome: what would you want from a sailing game?

comments.author: zeamp
comments.body: *If anything's going to happen, it's going to happen out there.*

comments.author: Kinami_
comments.body:
"Co-op is planned, and the game is built to support it from the start."

How do you build a game that has coop support from the start, yet coop is planned?

replies.author: GoneSailingDev
replies.body: The architecture is already built with that in mind, e.g. it already supports two characters on the boat. There's just no network code yet to let you join someone else's session.

comments.author: Romeowns
comments.body: If you could work in something like BeamNG Earth that would be wild. Would love to sail some local water with live weather.

replies.author: GoneSailingDev
replies.body: Yeah, that would be really wild, and I've had the same thought. Definitely something to look into long term, especially since every harbor would need to support docking. I haven't thought about live weather yet, great idea!

comments.author: GoneSailingDev
comments.body: Thank you a lot! And your game looks great! How did you create the water?

replies.author: redwolf1430
replies.body:
I am using unreal engine, and it was a crazy struggle with the water. I gave up trying to build my own and went with a plugin for the water. [https://www.fab.com/listings/0c1fc983-db84-4df3-b623-03db76d552c6?lang=en](https://www.fab.com/listings/0c1fc983-db84-4df3-b623-03db76d552c6?lang=en)

Which was also kind of a struggle to get what I want, especially the buoyancy. 

My goal was to build a world simulator with realistic weather and ocean conditions. So far I got the whole world in there with beautiful cities (Google's photogrammetry) Still working out some bugs with sea level around India and a few other places. Got auto pilot working. Last step will be to build in the sailing part and the mechanics. And model some better boats.

replies.author: GoneSailingDev
replies.body:
Combining your world simulator with my sailing physics and boat would’ve been awesome. Unfortunately I’m on Unity.

Once I get to the point of improving the water, I’m also worried about the struggle to get it right, so I’m thinking about going with a water asset like Crest.

replies.author: redwolf1430
replies.body: Nice what made you choose unity to build ?

replies.author: GoneSailingDev
replies.body: I looked at Godot, Unity, and Unreal. For a co-op 3D game, Unity and Unreal seemed like a better fit than Godot. I chose Unity over Unreal because coding tools seem to work better with it, and I already know C#.
